messages:
Caleb Johnson: circling back on streaming latency SLI: right now dashboards are mixing “time to first token” and “time to end” under one `latency_ms`. that’s going to be a mess for tiered SLOs. can we split TTFT vs end-to-end? and where do we want it emitted (gateway vs runtime)?

Aisha Bello: +1. for SLO we need something stable + user-perceived. TTFT is the thing users feel. “end-to-end stream duration” is super correlated with output length + client reading speed.

Aisha Bello: proposal from SRE side:
- Latency SLI for streaming = TTFT (p95 + p99)
- Separate “stream completion duration” as an ops metric, not the primary SLI, unless we normalize (e.g. ms/token)
- Keep disconnect rate as its own SLI

Amara Diallo: gateway can measure TTFT pretty cleanly (request received -> first chunk written). runtime can also measure (request admitted -> first token produced). those are NOT the same, so we should be explicit what “TTFT” means in SLI.

Nadia Rahman: agreed. also metering issues if we have both but dashboards pick whichever is “available”. we need canonical metric names + semantics.

Peter Holtz: if we only use gateway TTFT for SLI, we’ll miss cases where runtime is slow but gateway is buffering? (or vice versa). but for customer experience, gateway TTFT is closer.

Caleb Johnson: yeah. i’m leaning:
- SLI(TTFT) = gateway observation (customer-facing)
- Runtime emits its own TTFT as “internal breakdown” (queueing + compute)

Thomas Baird: before we add more metrics: can we keep label set under control? per-model + per-route + per-region + tier already hurts. if we add `{phase=ttft|e2e}` we at least avoid exploding metric count.

Aisha Bello: careful w/ `phase` as a label if it’s only 2 values it’s fine. the bigger issue is people adding `prompt_id` or `customer_id` etc. (nope)

Amara Diallo: semantics question: what is “end-to-end” for streaming?
1) request received -> last byte written
2) request received -> final token produced (even if client disconnected)
3) request received -> server closes stream

Amara Diallo: gateway can do (1) and (3). runtime can do (2) and also knows “tokens_generated”.

Mina Haddad: from routing POV, we care about “server time to produce first token” because it correlates with load / queue. but SLO should be customer-facing. so i’m good with dual metrics.

Nadia Rahman: for Dedicated customers, we’ve already had confusion where they say “TTFT is fine but responses are slow” — which is really token rate / total duration. might be worth having a second chart (not SLI) that shows `ms_per_token` or `tokens_per_sec`.

Peter Holtz: +1. total duration without normalizing is mostly “you asked for 2k tokens”. it will page constantly for long completions.

Caleb Johnson: ok, so we split into:
- `ttft_ms` (customer-facing SLI)
- `stream_duration_ms` (ops)
- `tokens_generated_total` (for normalization)
- optionally `tps` as a derived metric in dashboards

Aisha Bello: +1, and we should define TTFT precisely:
- For gateway: time from first byte read of request body (or headers received?) to first response chunk flush
- For runtime: time from “admitted to runtime” to first token produced

Aisha Bello: for the SLI doc, I’d rather define based on gateway because it includes queueing in gateway + routing + runtime. but excludes client network.

Amara Diallo: gateway timing points we have today:
- `req_start` when request enters handler
- `upstream_start` when we call routing
- `first_byte_sent` when first chunk is written
- `stream_closed` when response ends

Amara Diallo: we can emit two histograms:
```
redwood_gateway_stream_ttft_ms{tier,route,region,model}
redwood_gateway_stream_duration_ms{tier,route,region,model}
```
(and keep existing non-streaming `request_latency_ms` separate)

Thomas Baird: please don’t add `model` on gateway metrics if it’s not already there (cardinality). can we use `model_family` or `model_id` only for top N and aggregate rest?

Nadia Rahman: model dimension is required for SLO drilldowns, but we can compromise:
- keep `model` on “summary” metrics only (ttft + disconnect)
- for duration, aggregate to `model_family` or drop model

Aisha Bello: ^ this matches what we discussed in cardinality proposal: SLI metrics get the full dimension set; secondary metrics get reduced dims.

Caleb Johnson: runtime side: we already emit `redwood_runtime_decode_latency_ms` but it’s not tied to streaming boundaries. we need explicit “first token” marker.

Caleb Johnson: runtime can emit:
```
redwood_runtime_stream_ttft_ms{tier,route,region,model}
redwood_runtime_stream_total_compute_ms{tier,route,region,model}
redwood_runtime_stream_tokens_generated{tier,route,region,model}
```
then dashboards can show breakdown: gateway TTFT vs runtime TTFT.

Peter Holtz: what about “queue time” before runtime? i think control plane has it (scheduler wait). would be nice but can be phase 2.

Mina Haddad: routing can add `routing_decision_ms` and `fallback_taken` labels but that’s more dims. keep it simple for SLO.

Nadia Rahman: also: client aborts. if client disconnects early, gateway duration becomes short. we should not interpret that as “fast completion”. duration metric should only count completed streams.

Amara Diallo: yup. we already classify disconnects (499 vs server disconnect). for duration histogram we can emit only when `stream_status=completed`. for others, emit a counter for disconnect reason.

Aisha Bello: +1. from SLI standpoint:
- TTFT: include both completed + aborted (if the server managed to send first token)
- Duration: only completed
- Disconnect SLI: separate (server-side disconnects count as failures)

Thomas Baird: if we add `stream_status` label (completed/aborted/error) that’s 3 values; ok. but don’t add detailed reasons as labels; use a separate counter with controlled enum.

Caleb Johnson: action items:
1) Amara: gateway histograms for `stream_ttft_ms` and `stream_duration_ms` w/ `stream_status` gating duration on completed
2) Caleb: runtime emits `runtime_stream_ttft_ms` + tokens generated
3) Aisha/Nadia: update SLI spec to say SLO latency SLI for streaming = gateway TTFT (p95/p99). duration + tps are supporting.

Aisha Bello: works for me. i’ll also add note to SLO doc: for streaming endpoints we’ll show two latency panels in dashboards: TTFT and “tokens/sec” (derived). “end-to-end duration” stays as troubleshooting.

Amara Diallo: i’ll put up a draft PR today/tomorrow. will ping here for review.

Nadia Rahman: thanks. please make sure both metrics use same histogram buckets as standard (`[25,50,100,200,400,800,1600,3200,6400,10000]ms`) so queries don’t need special casing.

Caleb Johnson: :thumbsup: and we’ll keep naming consistent with non-streaming (`*_ms` histograms). will sync w/ Sergio on dashboards once emitted.

Peter Holtz: when this lands, can we also update canary analyzer to look at TTFT separately? today it flags “latency regression” on long responses.

Aisha Bello: yes, that’s the whole reason we’re doing this :)

Caleb Johnson: cool. i’ll link this thread in ENG-xxxx once i find the right ticket.
